title.zh: 卷一百五十九 列傳第四十六: 宋子貞 商挺 趙良弼 趙璧
title.en: Volume 159 Biographies 46: Song Zizhen, Shang Ting, Zhao Liangbi, Zhao Bi
title.raw: 卷一百五十九 列傳第四十六: 宋子貞 商挺 趙良弼 趙璧 Volume 159 Biographies 46: Song Zizhen, Shang Ting, Zhao Liangbi, Zhao Bi

sentences.zh: 宋子貞

translations.literal: Song Zizhen
translations.idiomatic: Song Zizhen

sentences.zh: 宋子貞，字周臣，潞州長子人也。

translations.literal: Song Zizhen, styled Zhouchen, was a native of Changzi in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zizhen, whose style name was Zhouchen, came from Changzi in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 性敏悟好學，工詞賦。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick-witted and fond of learning, and skilled in lyric poetry and rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally quick-witted and devoted to study, he excelled at regulated verse and fu.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，領薦書試禮部，與族兄知柔同補太學生，俱有名於時，人以大小宋稱之。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he received a recommendation and took the Ministry of Rites examination; he and his cousin Zhirou both entered the Imperial College and were both renowned at the time—people called them the Greater and Lesser Song.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he earned a recommendation and sat for the Ministry of Rites examination; he and his cousin Zhirou both entered the Imperial College and were celebrated in their day—people spoke of the Greater and Lesser Song.

sentences.zh: 金末，潞州亂，子貞走趙、魏間。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin, Luzhou was in turmoil, and Zizhen fled among Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin dynasty was collapsing, Luzhou fell into chaos, and Zizhen took refuge in the Zhao and Wei region.

sentences.zh: 宋將彭義斌守大名，辟為安撫司計議官。

translations.literal: The Song general Peng Yibin held Daming and recruited him as planning officer of the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Peng Yibin, who held Daming, appointed him planning officer of the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 義斌歿，子貞率眾歸東平行台嚴實。

translations.literal: When Yibin died, Zizhen led his followers to submit to Yan Shi of the Eastern Pacification Command.
translations.idiomatic: After Yibin died, Zizhen led his men to submit to Yan Shi of the Eastern Pacification Command.

sentences.zh: 實素聞其名，招置幕府，用為詳議官，兼提舉學校。

translations.literal: Shi had long heard his name, recruited him to his staff, used him as detailed deliberation officer, and also put him in charge of promoting schools.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had long known his reputation, brought him into his staff as a detailed deliberation officer, and also charged him with promoting schools.

sentences.zh: 先是，實每令人請事於朝，托近侍奏決，不經中書，因與丞相耶律楚材有違言。

translations.literal: Previously, Shi would often send people to petition the court on matters, entrust them to close attendants for decision without going through the Secretariat, and thereby had strained words with Chancellor Yelü Chucai.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Shi would often send men to petition the court and have matters decided through close attendants without routing them through the Secretariat, which put him at odds with Chancellor Yelü Chucai.

sentences.zh: 子貞至，勸實緻禮丞相，通殷勤，凡奏請，必先諮禀。

translations.literal: When Zizhen arrived, he urged Shi to send courtesy gifts to the chancellor and communicate goodwill; for every memorial request, he must first consult and report.
translations.idiomatic: When Zizhen arrived, he urged Shi to send proper courtesy to the chancellor and maintain cordial contact; every memorial had to be submitted for prior consultation.

sentences.zh: 丞相喜，自是交歡無間，實因此益委信子貞。

translations.literal: The chancellor was pleased; from then on their friendship was unbroken, and Shi therefore trusted Zizhen all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor was delighted, and from then on they were on the closest terms; Shi consequently relied on Zizhen even more.

sentences.zh: 太宗四年，實戍黃陵，金人悉力來攻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taizong, Shi garrisoned Huangling, and the Jin forces attacked with their full strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Taizong, Shi garrisoned Huangling, and the Jin army came against him with its full strength.

sentences.zh: 與戰不利，敵勢頗張，曹、濮以南皆震。

translations.literal: Battle went badly; the enemy's momentum grew strong, and the region south of Cao and Pu was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting went poorly, the enemy's power swelled, and the lands south of Cao and Pu were shaken.

sentences.zh: 有自敵中逃歸者，言金兵且大至，人情恟懼。

translations.literal: Some who escaped from the enemy said the Jin army would arrive in force soon; hearts were in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had fled from the enemy reported that the Jin army would soon arrive in strength, and panic spread.

sentences.zh: 子貞請於實，斬揚言者首以令諸城，境內乃安​​。

translations.literal: Zizhen asked Shi to behead the rumor-monger as an example to the cities, and the territory was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen asked Shi to execute the alarmist as a warning to the cities, and the region was calmed.

sentences.zh: 汴梁既下，饑民北徙，餓殍盈道。

translations.literal: After Bianliang fell, starving people moved north, and corpses of the starved filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: After Bianliang was taken, famine refugees streamed north, and the dead lay heaped along the roads.

sentences.zh: 子貞多方賑救，全活者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Zizhen rescued them by many means and saved more than ten thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen organized relief on many fronts and kept more than ten thousand people alive.

sentences.zh: 金士之流寓者，悉引見周給，且薦用之。

translations.literal: Jin scholars who were displaced he all summoned for audience, provided for them, and recommended them for employment.
translations.idiomatic: For Jin scholars adrift in exile he arranged audiences, supplied their needs, and recommended them for office.

sentences.zh: 拔名儒張特立、劉肅、李昶輩於羈旅，與之同列。

translations.literal: He drew eminent Confucians Zhang Teli, Liu Su, Li Chang, and others from their wanderings and ranked them alongside himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drew eminent scholars such as Zhang Teli, Liu Su, and Li Chang from their wanderings and treated them as peers.

sentences.zh: 四方之士聞風而至，故東平一時人材多於他鎮。

translations.literal: Scholars from the four directions came at the report of his fame, so at one time Dongping had more talent than other commands.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from every quarter came at his reputation, and for a time Dongping gathered more talent than any other command.

sentences.zh: 七年，太宗命子貞為行台右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Taizong appointed Zizhen right-section director of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Emperor Taizong appointed Zizhen director of the right section of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中原略定，事多草創，行台所統五十餘城，州縣之官或擢自將校，或起由民伍，率昧於從政。

translations.literal: The Central Plain was largely settled, but affairs were still being established from scratch; of the more than fifty cities under the branch, prefectural and county officials were sometimes promoted from military officers or raised from civilian ranks, and mostly ignorant of government.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain was largely pacified, yet institutions were still being improvised; the branch governed more than fifty cities, and prefectural and county officials were sometimes drawn from commanders or common soldiers, with little knowledge of administration.

sentences.zh: 甚者專以掊克聚斂為能，官吏相與為貪私以病民。

translations.literal: Some went so far as to make extortion and accumulation their sole talent; officials together practiced private greed to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: The worst made squeezing and hoarding their only skill, while officials colluded in private greed to afflict the people.

sentences.zh: 子貞仿前代觀察採訪之制，命官分三道糾察官吏，立為程式，與為期會，黜貪墯，獎廉勤，官府始有紀綱，民得蘇息。

translations.literal: Zizhen modeled the former dynasties' system of inspection and inquiry, ordered officials in three circuits to investigate administrators, set procedures and deadlines, dismissed the greedy and lazy, rewarded the incorrupt and diligent—and government at last had discipline, and the people could breathe.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen revived the former dynasties' touring inspection system, sent officers along three routes to investigate officials, set procedures and deadlines, dismissed the greedy and indolent, rewarded the upright and diligent—and government at last had order, and the people could recover.

sentences.zh: 東平將校，佔民為部曲戶，謂之腳寨，擅其賦役，幾四百所。

translations.literal: Dongping military officers had seized civilians as household troops called "foot stockades," monopolizing their taxes and corvée—nearly four hundred such places.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping commanders had seized civilians as household retainer bands called "foot stockades," monopolizing their taxes and corvée—nearly four hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 子貞請罷歸州縣。

translations.literal: Zizhen requested that these be abolished and returned to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen petitioned to abolish them and return the people to prefectural and county control.

sentences.zh: 實初難之，子貞力言乃聽，人以為便。

translations.literal: Shi at first found it difficult; after Zizhen spoke forcefully he consented, and people regarded it as a convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was reluctant at first, but after Zizhen pressed the point he agreed, and the people found it a great relief.

sentences.zh: 實卒，子忠濟襲爵，尤敬子貞。

translations.literal: When Shi died, his son Zhongji inherited the title and especially honored Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died, his son Zhongji inherited the fief and treated Zizhen with particular respect.

sentences.zh: 請於朝，授參議東平路事，兼提舉太常禮樂。

translations.literal: He petitioned the court and was appointed deliberator for Dongping Route affairs, also put in charge of the Directorate of Imperial Sacrifices and Court Music.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji petitioned the court to appoint him deliberator for Dongping Route affairs and superintendent of the Directorate of Imperial Sacrifices and Court Music.

sentences.zh: 子貞作新廟學，延前進士康曄、王磐為教官，招致生徒幾百人，出粟贍之，俾習經藝。

translations.literal: Zizhen built a new temple school, invited former jinshi Kang Ye and Wang Pan as instructors, gathered nearly four hundred students, issued grain to support them, and had them study the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen built a new temple school, invited former jinshi degree-holders Kang Ye and Wang Pan as instructors, gathered nearly four hundred students, issued grain to support them, and had them study the classics.

sentences.zh: 每季程試，必親臨之。

translations.literal: Every season's scheduled examination he personally attended.
translations.idiomatic: Each seasonal examination he attended in person.

sentences.zh: 齊魯儒風，為之一變。

translations.literal: Confucian teaching in Qi and Lu was thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian culture in Qi and Lu was transformed thereby.

sentences.zh: 歲己未，世祖南伐，召子貞至濮，問以方略。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei, Kublai Khan campaigned south and summoned Zizhen to Pu to ask his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In the year jiwei, Kublai Khan marched south and summoned Zizhen to Pu to ask his strategy.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「本朝威武有餘，仁德未洽。

translations.literal: He replied: "Our dynasty's martial might is more than sufficient, but benevolent virtue has not yet reached everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Our dynasty's martial prowess is more than enough, but benevolent rule has not yet won hearts everywhere.

sentences.zh: 所以拒命者，特畏死爾，若投降者不殺，脅從者勿治，則宋之郡邑，可傳檄而定也。」

translations.literal: Those who resist orders do so only because they fear death; if those who surrender are not killed and those compelled to follow are not punished, then the Song prefectures and cities can be taken by proclamation alone."
translations.idiomatic: Those who resist do so only because they fear death; if you do not kill those who surrender and do not punish those who were compelled to follow, the Song prefectures and cities can be won by proclamation alone."

sentences.zh: 世祖善其言。

translations.literal: The Khan thought well of his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，授益都路宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Yidu Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong he was made Pacification Commissioner of Yidu Route.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入覲，拜右三部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he entered court audience and was appointed Minister of the Right Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he came to court and was appointed Minister of the Right Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 時新立省部，典章制度，多子貞裁定。

translations.literal: At that time the new Secretariat and ministries were established, and most statutes and systems were decided by Zizhen.
translations.idiomatic: The new Secretariat and ministries were then being established, and most regulations were settled by Zizhen.

sentences.zh: 李璮叛，據濟南，詔子貞參議軍前行中書省事。

translations.literal: Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan; the emperor ordered Zizhen to deliberate on military affairs at the front Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan, the emperor ordered Zizhen to serve as deliberator on military affairs at the front Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子貞單騎至濟南，觀璮形勢，因說丞相史天澤曰：「璮擁眾東來，坐守孤城，宜增築外城，防其奔突，彼糧盡援絕，不攻自破矣。」

translations.literal: Zizhen rode alone to Jinan, observed Tan's situation, and said to Chancellor Shi Tianze: "Tan leads masses eastward but sits guarding a lone city; we should add an outer wall to prevent his breaking out—when his grain is gone and aid cut off, he will fall without attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen rode alone to Jinan, surveyed Tan's position, and told Chancellor Shi Tianze: "Tan has brought his host eastward yet sits in a lone city; we should build an outer wall to block his breakout—when his grain is exhausted and relief cut off, he will collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 議與天澤合，遂擒璮。

translations.literal: The plan accorded with Tianze's, and Tan was captured."
translations.idiomatic: The plan matched Tianze's thinking, and Tan was captured."

sentences.zh: 子貞還，上書陳便宜十事，大略謂：「官爵人主之柄，選法宜盡歸吏部。

translations.literal: Zizhen returned and memorialized ten measures of convenience, in gist: "Offices and ranks are the sovereign's power—the selection method should wholly return to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen returned and submitted ten practical recommendations, in summary: "Rank and office are the sovereign's prerogative; the selection process should be returned entirely to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 律令國之紀綱，宜早刊定。

translations.literal: Laws and ordinances are the state's guideline and should be published early.
translations.idiomatic: Laws and ordinances are the state's backbone and should be promulgated without delay.

sentences.zh: 監司總統一路，用非其材，不厭人望，乞選公廉有才德者為之。

translations.literal: Circuit overseers govern a whole route—when unfit men are used, popular expectation is unsatisfied; I beg to select those of integrity, talent, and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit overseers govern entire routes; when unfit men are appointed, public trust is betrayed—I beg that upright men of talent and virtue be chosen.

sentences.zh: 今州縣官相傳以世，非法賦斂，民窮無告，宜遷轉以革其弊。」

translations.literal: Today prefectural and county officers pass posts hereditarily, levy illegal taxes, and the people are destitute with nowhere to appeal—posts should rotate to reform this abuse."
translations.idiomatic: Today prefectural and county offices pass from father to son, illegal levies ruin the people, and there is no redress—officials should be rotated to break this abuse."

sentences.zh: 又請建國學教冑子，敕州郡提學課試諸生，三年一貢舉。

translations.literal: He also asked to establish a National University to teach the emperor's sons, order prefectures and circuits to promote learning and examine students, and hold triennial tribute and recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to establish a National University to educate the imperial sons, order prefectures and circuits to promote learning and examine students, and hold triennial tribute examinations.

sentences.zh: 有旨命中書次第施行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to implement these step by step.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Secretariat to carry these out in order.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，始罷州縣官世襲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, hereditary prefectural and county offices were at last abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan, hereditary prefectural and county offices were finally abolished.

sentences.zh: 遣子貞與左丞相耶律鑄行山東，遷調所部官。

translations.literal: Zizhen was sent with Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu to travel Shandong and transfer officials of the region.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhen was dispatched with Left Chancellor Yelü Zhu to tour Shandong and reassign its officials.

sentences.zh: 還，授翰林學士，參議中書省事。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Hanlin Academician and deliberator of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Hanlin Academician and deliberator of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 奏請班俸祿，定職田，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to schedule salary stipends and fix official fields—the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to institute graded salaries and assign official fields, and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 复陳時務之切要者十二策。

translations.literal: Again he presented twelve policies on pressing current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted twelve policies on urgent matters of state.

sentences.zh: 帝頗悔用子貞晚。

translations.literal: The emperor rather regretted employing Zizhen late.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted that he had not employed Zizhen sooner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以年老求退，帝曰：「卿氣力未衰，勉為朕留，措置大事，俟百司差有條理，聽卿自便。」

translations.literal: Before long, citing age he sought retirement; the emperor said: "Your strength is not yet spent—strive to remain for Us, dispose great affairs; when the hundred offices have some order, We shall let you do as you will.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, pleading age, he sought to retire; the emperor said: "Your vigor is not yet spent—stay on for Us and manage great affairs; when the hundred offices are somewhat in order, We shall let you go as you wish.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，懇辭，乃得請。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year he pleaded earnestly and was permitted to leave."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year he pressed his request earnestly and was granted leave."

sentences.zh: 特敕中書，凡有大事，即其家訪問。

translations.literal: A special edict to the Secretariat: for any great matter, go to his home to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict to the Secretariat directed that for any major affair they should seek his counsel at home.

sentences.zh: 子貞私居，每聞朝廷事不便，必封疏上奏，愛君憂國，不以進退異其心。

translations.literal: In private life, whenever he heard that court affairs were ill-advised he would seal a memorial to the throne; love of the ruler and care for the state did not change with advance or withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement, whenever he heard that court policy was misguided he would seal a memorial; his devotion to the ruler and concern for the state did not waver with rank or withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 始病，家人進醫藥，卻之曰：「死生有命，吾年逾八十，何以藥為！」

translations.literal: When illness began, his family brought medicine; he refused: "Life and death have their allotment—I am over eighty; what need of drugs!
translations.idiomatic: When he first fell ill his family offered medicine; he refused it, saying: "Life and death are fated—I am past eighty; what use are drugs!

sentences.zh: 病危，諸子請遺言，子貞曰：「吾平昔教汝者不少，今尚何言耶！」

translations.literal: When critically ill his sons asked for last words; Zizhen said: "In ordinary times I have taught you enough—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: As his condition worsened his sons asked for a final charge; Zizhen said: "I have taught you enough in ordinary times—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 子渤，字齊彥，有才名，官至集賢學士。

translations.literal: His son Bo, styled Qiyan, had a reputation for talent and rose to Academician of the Hall of Collected Glories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bo, styled Qiyan, was known for talent and rose to Academician of the Hall of Collected Glories.

sentences.zh: 商挺

translations.literal: Shang Ting
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ting

sentences.zh: 商挺，字孟卿，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Shang Ting, styled Mengqing, was a man of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ting, whose style name was Mengqing, was from Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 其先本姓殷氏，避宋諱改焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors had the surname Yin; they changed it to avoid the Song taboo.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears bore the surname Yin and changed it to avoid the Song imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 父衡，僉陝西行省員外郎，以戰死。

translations.literal: His father Heng was a Yuanwai Lang of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heng served as Yuanwai Lang of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 挺年二十四，汴京破，北走，依冠氏趙天錫，與元好問、楊奐遊。

translations.literal: When Ting was twenty-four, Bianjing fell; he fled north, attached himself to Zhao Tianxi of Guanshi, and associated with Yuan Haowen and Yang Huan.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four, when Bianjing fell, he fled north, joined Zhao Tianxi of Guanshi, and kept company with Yuan Haowen and Yang Huan.

sentences.zh: 東平嚴實聘為諸子師。

translations.literal: Yan Shi of Dongping hired him as tutor to his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi of Dongping engaged him as tutor to his sons.

sentences.zh: 實卒，子忠濟嗣，辟挺為經歷，出為曹州判官。

translations.literal: When Shi died, his son Zhongji succeeded; Ting was recruited as administrator, then went out as Caozhou judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died, his son Zhongji succeeded; Ting was recruited as administrator, then served as judge of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為經歷，贊忠濟興學養士。

translations.literal: Before long he was again administrator and supported Zhongji in promoting learning and nurturing scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again administrator and helped Zhongji promote learning and nurture scholars.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，世祖在潛邸，受京兆分地，聞挺名，遣使徵至鹽州。

translations.literal: In the year guichou, Kublai Khan was in his princely establishment and received the Jingzhao allotment; hearing Ting's name, he sent envoys to summon him to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the year guichou, while Kublai Khan was still in his princely establishment and had received the Jingzhao allotment, he heard of Ting's reputation and sent envoys to summon him to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 入對稱旨，字而不名。

translations.literal: His audience answers pleased the Khan, who called him by his style name without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: His answers at audience pleased the Khan, who addressed him by his style name and did not use his personal name.

sentences.zh: 間陪宴語，因曰：「挺來時，李璮城朐山，東平當饋米萬石。

translations.literal: Once during a banquet he said: "When Ting came, Li Tan held Tushan; Dongping was to supply ten thousand piculs of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet he remarked: "When I came, Li Tan held Tushan and Dongping was ordered to deliver ten thousand piculs of rice.

sentences.zh: 東平至朐山，率十石致一石，且車淖於雨，必後期，後期罪死。

translations.literal: From Dongping to Tushan, ten piculs sent yielded one picul delivered, and carts bogged in rain—surely they would miss the deadline, and missing the deadline meant death.
translations.idiomatic: From Dongping to Tushan, ten piculs dispatched yielded one picul received; carts mired in rain would miss the deadline, and missing the deadline meant death.

sentences.zh: 請輸沂州，使璮軍取食，便。」

translations.literal: Please have it delivered to Yizhou so Tan's army could take food there—more convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Please route the grain to Yizhou and let Tan's army draw supplies there—it would be far easier."

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「愛民如此，忍不卿從。」

translations.literal: The Khan said: "Caring for the people like this—how could I bear not to have you follow."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "To care for the people like this—how could I not have you at my side."

sentences.zh: 楊惟中宣撫關中，挺為郎中。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong pacified Guanzhong; Ting served as Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Weizhong pacified Guanzhong, Ting served as Langzhong under him.

sentences.zh: 兵火之餘，八州十二縣，戶不滿萬，皆驚憂無聊。

translations.literal: After the fires of war, eight prefectures and twelve counties had fewer than ten thousand households altogether—all anxious and without resource.
translations.idiomatic: After the devastation of war, eight prefectures and twelve counties together counted fewer than ten thousand households—everywhere people were fearful and destitute.

sentences.zh: 挺佐惟中，進賢良，黜貪暴，明尊卑，出淹滯，定規程，主簿責，印楮幣，頒俸祿，務農薄稅，通其有無。

translations.literal: Ting assisted Weizhong in advancing the worthy, dismissing the greedy and violent, clarifying honor and rank, releasing the long detained, fixing regulations, holding registrars responsible, issuing paper currency, distributing salaries, promoting agriculture and lightening taxes, and circulating goods where there were surpluses and shortages.
translations.idiomatic: Ting assisted Weizhong in advancing the worthy, removing the greedy and violent, clarifying ranks, releasing the long detained, setting regulations, enforcing registrar accountability, issuing paper currency, distributing salaries, promoting farming and easing taxes, and moving goods from surplus to shortage.

sentences.zh: 期月，民乃安。

translations.literal: Within a month the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 誅一大猾，群吏咸懼。

translations.literal: They executed one great rascal and all clerks were in fear.
translations.idiomatic: They executed one powerful scoundrel, and every clerk trembled.

sentences.zh: 且請減關中常賦之半。

translations.literal: They also requested to halve the standing tax of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They also petitioned to cut Guanzhong's regular tax by half.

sentences.zh: 明年，惟中罷，廉希憲來代，升挺為宣撫副使。

translations.literal: The next year Weizhong was dismissed; Lian Xixian came in his stead and promoted Ting to Vice Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Weizhong was replaced; Lian Xixian took over and promoted Ting to Vice Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，徵京兆軍需布萬匹、米三千石、帛三千段，械器稱是，輸平涼軍。

translations.literal: In bingchen year they levied from Jingzhao ten thousand bolts of cloth for army needs, three thousand piculs of rice, three thousand bolts of silk, and weapons in proportion, to supply Pingliang army.
translations.idiomatic: In bingchen the court levied on Jingzhao ten thousand bolts of cloth for army needs, three thousand piculs of rice, three thousand bolts of silk, and a proportional quantity of arms, all for the Pingliang army.

sentences.zh: 期迫甚，郡人大恐。

translations.literal: The deadline was very urgent and the commandery was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The deadline was crushing and the commandery was in terror.

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「他易集也，運米千里，妨我蠶麥。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "The other items are easy to collect; transporting grain a thousand li would harm our silkworms and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "The other requisitions are easy to meet; hauling grain a thousand li would ruin our silkworm season and wheat harvest.

sentences.zh: 郿長王姓者，平涼人也，挺召與謀，對曰：「不煩官運，僕家有積粟，請以代輸。」

translations.literal: A Wang from Meixian, a native of Pingliang, was summoned to counsel; he answered: "No need for official transport—your servant's family has stored grain; please let me deliver in your stead."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a Mr. Wang of Meixian, a native of Pingliang, to consult; Wang replied: "No need for official transport—my family has grain in store; let me deliver it in your stead."

sentences.zh: 挺大悅，載價與之，他輸亦如期。

translations.literal: Ting was greatly pleased, loaded the price and gave it to him; the other deliveries also met the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was delighted, loaded the payment and gave it to him, and the other deliveries also met their deadlines.

sentences.zh: 復命兼治懷孟，境內大治。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to administer Huaimei as well—the territory was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He was again charged with Huaimei as well, and the region was thoroughly well governed.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，憲宗命阿藍答兒會計河南、陝右。

translations.literal: In dingwei year Möngke ordered Alan Dar to audit Henan and Shaanxi right.
translations.idiomatic: In dingwei Emperor Möngke ordered Alan Dar to audit Henan and the right bank of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 戊午，罷宣撫司，挺還東平。

translations.literal: In wuwu year the Pacification Commission was abolished; Ting returned to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu the Pacification Commission was abolished and Ting returned to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 憲宗親征蜀，世祖將趨鄂、漢，軍於小濮，召問軍事。

translations.literal: Möngke personally campaigned in Shu; the Khan was to advance toward E and Han, encamped at Xiaopu, and summoned him to ask about military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke campaigned in person in Shu; the Khan was to march on E and Han and encamped at Xiaopu, summoning Ting to ask about military affairs.

sentences.zh: 挺對曰​​：「蜀道險遠，萬乘豈宜輕動。」

translations.literal: Ting replied: "The Shu road is perilous and far—how should the myriad-chariot lord lightly move."
translations.idiomatic: Ting answered: "The road into Shu is treacherous and remote—how should the Son of Heaven lightly take the field."

sentences.zh: 世祖默然久之，曰：「卿言正契吾心。」

translations.literal: The Khan was silent a long time and said: "Your words match my heart exactly."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan was silent a long while, then said: "Your words are exactly what is in my heart."

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩，世祖北還，道遣張文謙與挺計事。

translations.literal: Möngke died; the Khan returned north and on the road sent Zhang Wenqian and Ting to plan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke died the Khan turned north; on the march he sent Zhang Wenqian and Ting ahead to plan affairs.

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「軍中當嚴符信，以防奸詐。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "In the army tokens and credentials should be strictly observed to guard against treachery."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "In the army, tallies and credentials must be strictly enforced to guard against treachery."

sentences.zh: 文謙急追及言之。

translations.literal: Wenqian hurriedly pursued and overtook him to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian spurred after him in haste and reported this.

sentences.zh: 世祖大悟，罵曰：「無一人為我言此，非商孟卿幾敗大計！」

translations.literal: The Khan awoke greatly and cursed: "Not one person told me this—had it not been for Shang Mengqing we would nearly have ruined the great plan!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khan came to himself with a start and exclaimed: "Not one of you told me this—had it not been for Shang Mengqing we would nearly have wrecked the great design!"

sentences.zh: 速遣使至軍立約。

translations.literal: He quickly sent envoys to the army to establish agreements.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent envoys to the army to set the agreements in place.

sentences.zh: 未幾，阿里不哥之使至軍中，執而斬之。

translations.literal: Before long, Ariq Böke's envoys reached the army; they were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ariq Böke's envoys arrived at the army and were seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 召挺北上至開平，挺與廉希憲密贊大計。

translations.literal: Ting was summoned north to Kaiping; he and Lian Xixian secretly advised on the great design.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was summoned north to Kaiping, where he and Lian Xixian privately counseled on the great succession plan.

sentences.zh: 世祖既即位，挺奏曰：「南師宜還扈乘輿，西師宜軍便地。」

translations.literal: After the Khan took the throne, Ting memorialized: "The southern army should return to guard the imperial carriage; the western army should encamp where convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the Khan received Ting's memorial: "The southern force should return to guard the imperial carriage; the western force should hold ground where it is advantageous."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 以廉希憲及挺宣撫陝、蜀。

translations.literal: Lian Xixian and Ting were appointed to pacify Shaanxi and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Xixian and Ting were charged to pacify Shaanxi and Shu.

sentences.zh: 中統元年夏五月，至京兆。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the first year of Zhongtong they reached Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer of the first year of Zhongtong they arrived at Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花者，徵蜀時名將也，渾都海嘗為之副，時駐六盤山，以兵應阿里不哥。

translations.literal: Harabucha was a famed general of the Shu campaign; Hüntaihai had once been his deputy and now garrisoned Liupanshan with troops to support Ariq Böke.
translations.idiomatic: Harabucha had been a celebrated general in the Shu campaign; Hüntaihai, who had served under him, now held Liupanshan with forces answering Ariq Böke.

sentences.zh: 挺謂希憲曰：「為六盤，有三策。

translations.literal: Ting said to Xixian: "For Liupanshan there are three strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Ting told Xixian: "Regarding Liupanshan, there are three courses.

sentences.zh: 悉銳而東，直搗京兆，上策也；

translations.literal: Lead all elite forces east and strike straight at Jingzhao—the best strategy;
translations.idiomatic: The best: concentrate every crack troop and drive east straight at Jingzhao;

sentences.zh: 聚兵六盤，觀釁而動，中策也；

translations.literal: mass troops at Liupanshan and move when opportunity appears—the middle strategy;
translations.idiomatic: The middle: mass at Liupanshan and watch for an opening;

sentences.zh: 重裝北歸，以應和林，下策也。」

translations.literal: return north with heavy baggage to join Qara Qorum—the worst strategy."
translations.idiomatic: The worst: haul heavy stores north to join Qara Qorum."

sentences.zh: 希憲曰：「彼將何從？」

translations.literal: Xixian said: "Which will they take?"
translations.idiomatic: Xixian asked: "Which will they choose?"

sentences.zh: 挺曰：「必出下策。」

translations.literal: Ting said: "They will surely take the worst."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "They will certainly take the worst."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 於是與希憲定議，令八春、汪良臣發兵御之，事具《希憲傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Xixian decided to order Bachu and Wang Liangchen to raise troops to resist them—the details are in Xixian's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xixian then ordered Bachu and Wang Liangchen to take the field against them, as set out in Xixian's biography.

sentences.zh: 六盤之兵既北，而阿藍答兒自和林引兵南來，與哈剌不花、渾都海遇於甘州。

translations.literal: Once the Liupanshan army had gone north, Alan Dar led troops south from Qara Qorum and met Harabucha and Hüntaihai at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liupanshan force marched north, Alan Dar led an army south from Qara Qorum and joined Harabucha and Hüntaihai at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花以語不合，引其兵北去，阿藍答兒遂與渾都海合軍而南。

translations.literal: Harabucha, disagreeing in counsel, led his troops north away; Alan Dar then united with Hüntaihai and marched south.
translations.idiomatic: Harabucha, quarreling with Alan Dar, withdrew north with his men; Alan Dar then combined with Hüntaihai and advanced south.

sentences.zh: 時諸王合丹率騎兵與八春、汪良臣兵合，乃分為三道以拒之。

translations.literal: Prince Hüdan then led cavalry to join Bachu and Wang Liangchen's forces, and they divided into three routes to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hüdan brought his cavalry to join Bachu and Wang Liangchen, and they arrayed in three columns to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 既陣，大風吹沙，良臣令軍士下馬，以短兵突其左，繞出陣後，潰其右而出，八春直搗其前，合丹勒精騎邀其歸路，大戰於甘州東，殺阿藍答兒、渾都海。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, a great wind blew sand; Liangchen ordered the men to dismount and with short weapons burst their left, wheel behind the formation, break their right and emerge, Bachu struck their front straight on, and Hüdan led elite cavalry to cut their retreat—at a great battle east of Ganzhou Alan Dar and Hüntaihai were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the lines clashed, a sandstorm rose; Liangchen had his men dismount and with short weapons smash the enemy left, swing behind the formation and rout the right, Bachu hit them head-on, and Hüdan barred their retreat with picked cavalry—in the great battle east of Ganzhou Alan Dar and Hüntaihai were slain.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝大悅，曰：「商孟卿，古之良將也。」

translations.literal: When word reached the throne, the emperor was greatly pleased and said: "Shang Mengqing is a general of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived, the emperor rejoiced and said: "Shang Mengqing is a commander of the old school."

sentences.zh: 改宣撫司為行中書省，進希憲為右丞，挺為僉行省事。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission was changed to a Branch Secretariat; Xixian was promoted to Right Chancellor and Ting to Associate Director of Branch Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission became a Branch Secretariat; Xixian was made Right Chancellor and Ting Associate Director of Branch Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，進參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Vice Director of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted Vice Director of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 宋將劉整以滬州降，系前降宋者數百人來歸，軍吏請誅以戒，挺盡奏而釋之。

translations.literal: The Song general Liu Zheng surrendered Huzhou and brought several hundred former Song men in bonds; the army officers asked to execute them as a warning, but Ting memorialized to release them all.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Liu Zheng surrendered Huzhou he brought several hundred earlier Song defectors in bonds; officers wanted them executed as a warning, but Ting memorialized for their full release.

sentences.zh: 興元判官費寅有罪懼誅，以藉兵完城事訟挺與希憲於朝。

translations.literal: The Xingyuan judge Fei Yin, fearing punishment for a crime, sued Ting and Xixian at court on the matter of requisitioning troops to repair the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The Xingyuan judge Fei Yin, guilty and fearing death, accused Ting and Xixian at court of press-ganging labor to complete the city walls.

sentences.zh: 帝召挺便殿，問曰：「卿在關中、懷孟，兩著治效，而毀言日至，豈同寅有沮卿者耶？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Ting to the informal hall and asked: "You achieved good governance in Guanzhong and Huaimei, yet slander reaches Us daily—is it that Yin and his kind obstruct you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Ting to the informal audience and asked: "You governed Guanzhong and Huaimei well, yet calumny reaches Us every day—is it that Yin and men like him stand in your way?

sentences.zh: 抑位高而志怠耶？

translations.literal: Or that your rank is high and your will slack?
translations.idiomatic: Or that high office has dulled your purpose?

sentences.zh: 比年論王文統者甚眾，卿獨無一言。」

translations.literal: In recent years many have denounced Wang Wentong, yet you alone have not spoken a word."
translations.idiomatic: These years many have denounced Wang Wentong, yet you alone have said nothing."

sentences.zh: 挺對曰：「臣素知文統之為人，嘗與趙璧論之，想陛下猶能記也。

translations.literal: Ting replied: "Your servant has long known Wentong's character and once discussed him with Zhao Bi—I trust Your Majesty still remembers.
translations.idiomatic: Ting answered: "I have long known Wentong's character and once discussed him with Zhao Bi—Your Majesty may still recall it.

sentences.zh: 臣在秦三年，多過，其或從權以應變者有之。

translations.literal: Your servant was three years in Qin and committed many faults; there were times he bent rules to meet emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: I served three years in Qin and erred often; at times I bent rules to meet emergencies.

sentences.zh: 若功成以歸己，事敗分咎於人，臣必不敢，請就戮。」

translations.literal: But to claim success for himself and lay blame on others when things failed—Your servant would never dare; I beg to accept execution."
translations.idiomatic: Yet to take credit when things succeeded and shift blame when they failed—I would never dare; I beg to accept punishment."

sentences.zh: 挺既出，帝顧駙馬忽剌出、樞副合答等，數挺前後大計，凡十有七，因歎曰：「挺有功如是，猶自言有罪，若此，誰復為朕戮力耶！

translations.literal: After Ting withdrew, the emperor turned to the imperial son-in-law Hulachu, Vice Director Heda, and others, recounting seventeen of Ting's great designs in succession, and sighed: "Ting has served thus and still calls himself guilty—if such men will not strive for Us, who will!
translations.idiomatic: When Ting had left, the emperor turned to the imperial son-in-law Hulachu, Vice Director Heda, and others, listing seventeen of Ting's major plans in order, and sighed: "Ting has done so much yet still claims guilt—if men like this will not exert themselves for Us, who will!

sentences.zh: 卿等識之。」

translations.literal: Take note of this."
translations.idiomatic: Mark this well."

sentences.zh: 四年，賜金符，行四川行樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was granted a gold tally and acted as Sichuan Branch Privy Council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was granted a gold tally and directed Sichuan Branch Privy Council affairs.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，入拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan he entered court and was appointed Vice Director of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan he entered court and was made Vice Director of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 建議史事，附修遼、金二史，宜令王鶚、李治、徐世隆、高鳴、胡祗遹、周砥等為之，甚合帝意。

translations.literal: He proposed that in compiling history, the Liao and Jin histories should be appended, and that Wang E, Li Zhi, Xu Shilong, Gao Ming, Hu Zhiyuan, Zhou Di, and others undertake it—this greatly pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that the histories of Liao and Jin be undertaken alongside the main history, with Wang E, Li Zhi, Xu Shilong, Gao Ming, Hu Zhiyuan, Zhou Di, and others as compilers, which greatly pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 二年，分省河東，俄召還。

translations.literal: In the second year he was assigned to the Hedong Branch Secretariat; soon he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was sent to the Hedong Branch Secretariat and soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝留意經學，挺與姚樞、竇默、王鶚、楊果纂《五經要語》凡二十八類以進。

translations.literal: In the third year, as the emperor turned his mind to the classics, Ting joined Yao Shu, Dou Mo, Wang E, and Yang Guo in compiling Essential Sayings of the Five Classics in twenty-eight categories and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the emperor devoted attention to the classics, Ting joined Yao Shu, Dou Mo, Wang E, and Yang Guo in compiling Essential Passages of the Five Classics in twenty-eight categories and presented them.

sentences.zh: 六年，同僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as Associate Privy Council Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was Associate Privy Council Director.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷僉書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Privy Council Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Privy Council Secretary.

sentences.zh: 八年，升副使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 數軍食，定軍官品級，給軍吏俸。

translations.literal: He tallied army provisions, fixed military officer grades, and granted salaries to army clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He audited army rations, fixed military officer grades, and instituted salaries for army clerks.

sentences.zh: 使四千人屯田，開懇三萬畝，收其獲以餉親軍。

translations.literal: He had four thousand men open fields and reclaimed thirty thousand mu, using the harvest to feed the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: He put four thousand men to farming, opened thirty thousand mu of wasteland, and used the yield to supply the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 汰不勝軍者戶三萬戶，一丁者亦汰去；

translations.literal: He eliminated thirty thousand households unfit for military service, and households with only one able man were also struck off;
translations.idiomatic: He struck thirty thousand households unfit for service from the rolls, and single-male households were removed as well;

sentences.zh: 丁多業寡，業多丁寡，財力相資，合出一軍。

translations.literal: where many sons had little land or much land had few sons, wealth and labor were pooled so that together they furnished one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: where many sons had little property or much property had few sons, households were grouped so wealth and labor together supplied one soldier.

sentences.zh: 初，運使郭琮、郎中郭叔雲與王相趙炳構隙。

translations.literal: Initially the transport commissioner Guo Cong and Langzhong Guo Shuyun had a feud with Chancellor Zhao Bing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Transport Commissioner Guo Cong and Langzhong Guo Shuyun were at odds with Chancellor Zhao Bing.

sentences.zh: 或告炳不法，妃命囚之六盤獄以死。

translations.literal: Someone reported Bing's illegal conduct; the consort ordered him imprisoned in the Liupanshan jail to die.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported Bing's misconduct; the consort ordered him imprisoned in the Liupanshan jail to die there.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑擅殺之，執琮、叔雲鞫問，伏辜，事具《趙炳傳》。

translations.literal: The court suspected unauthorized killing; Cong and Shuyun were arrested and interrogated, confessed guilt—the details are in Bing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspected unauthorized execution; Cong and Shuyun were seized and examined, confessed—the account is in Bing's biography.

sentences.zh: 初無一毫及挺。

translations.literal: At first not a thread involved Ting.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ting was not implicated in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 惟王府女奚徹徹，以預二郭謀，臨刑，望以求生，始有曖昧語連挺及其子讞。

translations.literal: Only the princely household maid Cheche, who had joined the two Guos' plot, at execution looked about hoping to live and then made ambiguous statements linking Ting and his son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Only the princely household maid Cheche, who had shared the two Guos' conspiracy, at execution glanced about hoping for life and then made vague statements implicating Ting and his son Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召挺​​，拘炳家，瓛下獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, summoned Ting, detained Bing's household, and Yan was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, summoned Ting, sealed Bing's household, and Yan was cast into prison.

sentences.zh: 帝命趙氏子曰：「商孟卿，老書生，可與諸儒讞其罪。」

translations.literal: The emperor told Zhao's son: "Shang Mengqing is an old scholar—have the Confucians debate his crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhao's son: "Shang Mengqing is an old scholar—let the Ru debate his offense."

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書青陽夢炎以議勳奏曰：「臣宋儒，不知挺向來之功可補今之過否？」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Qingyang Mengyan memorialized on merit: "Your servant is a Song Ru—does he not know whether Ting's past service can offset today's fault?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Qingyang Mengyan argued on merit: "I am a Song Ru and do not know whether Ting's former service can redeem his present fault."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅曰：「是同類相助之辭也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "That is the language of men aiding their own kind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, said: "That is how men of one party speak for each other."

sentences.zh: 符寶郎董文忠奏曰：「夢炎不知挺何如人，臣以曩時推戴之功語之矣。」

translations.literal: Keeper of Seals Dong Wenzong memorialized: "Mengyan does not know what manner of man Ting is—Your servant has told him of his merit in the days of raising the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Keeper of Seals Dong Wenzong said: "Mengyan does not know Ting's worth—I have already spoken to him of his service in the founding days."

sentences.zh: 帝良久曰：「其事果何如？」

translations.literal: After a long silence the emperor said: "How did the matter truly stand?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor asked: "How did the matter truly stand?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣目未睹，耳固聞之，殺人之謀，挺不與也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your servant did not see with his eyes but heard with his ears—Ting had no part in a plot to kill."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I did not see with my own eyes, but I have heard that Ting took no part in murder."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，有旨：挺不可全以無罪釋之，籍其家。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixteenth year an edict directed that Ting could not be released wholly without guilt—his property was registered.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the sixteenth year an edict held that Ting could not be released entirely innocent—his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 是冬，始釋挺及讞。

translations.literal: That winter Ting and Yan were at last released.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Ting and Yan were finally released.

sentences.zh: 二十年，复樞密副使，俄以疾免。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was again Vice Director of the Privy Council but soon resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was again Privy Council Vice Director but soon resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，趙氏子復訟父冤，挺又被系，百餘日乃釋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Zhao's son again sued over his father's wrong; Ting was again detained more than a hundred days before release.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Zhao's son again sued over his father's grievance; Ting was again held more than a hundred days before release.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，帝問中丞董文用曰：「商孟卿今年幾何？」

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor asked Censor-in-Chief Dong Wenyong: "How old is Shang Mengqing now?"
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor asked Censor-in-Chief Dong Wenyong: "How old is Shang Mengqing?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「八十。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Eighty."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Eighty."

sentences.zh: 帝甚惜其老，而歎其康強。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly prized his age yet marveled at his vigor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his great age yet marveled at his strength.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬十有二月卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of winter that year.

sentences.zh: 有詩千餘篇，尤善隸書。

translations.literal: He left more than a thousand poems and was especially skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than a thousand poems and excelled at clerical script.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，贈推誠協謀佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、魯國公，諡文定。

translations.literal: In the early Yanyou era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Meritorious Minister Who Sincerely Assists in Planning and Supporting the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with the privilege of opening a government office, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Lu, with the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yanyou period he was posthumously enfeoffed Meritorious Minister of Sincere Counsel Who Assisted the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with privilege to open an office, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Lu, posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 子五人：琥、璘、瑭、瓛、琦。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Hu, Lin, Tang, Yan, and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Hu, Lin, Tang, Yan, and Qi.

sentences.zh: 琥字台符。

translations.literal: Hu, styled Taifu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, whose style was Taifu.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，以姚樞、許衡薦，拜江南行御史臺監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation of Yao Shu and Xu Heng, he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, on the recommendation of Yao Shu and Xu Heng, he was made Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 建康戍卒有利湯氏財者，投戈於其家，誣為反具。

translations.literal: A Jiankang garrison soldier coveted the Tang clan's wealth, cast a weapon into their house, and framed them for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiankang garrison soldier coveted the Tang family's wealth, threw a weapon into their house, and accused them of treason.

sentences.zh: 琥知其冤，罪誣者而釋之。

translations.literal: Hu knew they were wronged, punished the accuser, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu saw they were innocent, punished the false accuser, and freed them.

sentences.zh: 華亭蟠龍寺僧思月謀叛被擒，其黨縱火來劫，民大擾，琥亟誅其魁。

translations.literal: The monk Siyue of Panlong Temple in Huating plotted rebellion and was captured; his followers set fires to raid and the people were greatly disturbed—Hu swiftly executed the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The Huating Panlong Temple monk Siyue plotted rebellion and was seized; his band set fires to loot and the people were in uproar—Hu quickly executed the leaders.

sentences.zh: 文法吏責琥擅誅，行台中丞張雄飛曰：「江南殘毀之餘，盜賊屢起，顧尚循常例，安用憲台為哉！」

translations.literal: Legal clerks blamed Hu for unauthorized execution; Branch Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xiongfei said: "South of the Yangtze is still in ruins and bandits rise again and again—if we still cling to routine, what use is a censorate!"
translations.idiomatic: Legal officers charged Hu with unauthorized killing; Branch Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xiongfei said: "The south is still shattered and bandits rise repeatedly—if we cling to routine, what need is there for a censorate!"

sentences.zh: 吏議遂屈。

translations.literal: The clerks' argument was thereby defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks' case collapsed.

sentences.zh: 都昌妖賊杜萬一，僭號倡亂，行台檄琥按問。

translations.literal: The Du Wanyi of Duchang, a demonic rebel who usurped title and raised disorder—the Branch Secretariat ordered Hu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Duchang demonic rebel Du Wanyi usurped a title and raised revolt; the Branch Secretariat ordered Hu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 械系脅從者盈獄，琥悉以詿誤縱遣之。

translations.literal: Coerced followers filled the prisons in chains; Hu released them all as misled.
translations.idiomatic: Followers seized under coercion filled the jails; Hu released them all as misled.

sentences.zh: 黨與竄伏者猶眾，琥揭榜招徠，不三日雲集。

translations.literal: Many accomplices still lurked in hiding; Hu posted notices to summon them, and within three days they gathered in clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Many accomplices still hid in the hills; Hu posted proclamations to summon them, and in less than three days they came in crowds.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，徵拜中台監察御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was summoned as Investigating Censor of the Central Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was summoned as Investigating Censor of the Central Censorate.

sentences.zh: 屬地震，琥上書言：「昔漢文帝有此異，而無其應，蓋以躬行德化而弭也。」

translations.literal: When an earthquake occurred, Hu memorialized: "In Han Wendi's time there was this omen yet no disaster followed—because he practiced virtue himself and stilled it."
translations.idiomatic: When an earthquake struck, Hu memorialized: "Under Emperor Wen of Han this omen appeared yet brought no calamity—because he practiced virtue himself and stilled it."

sentences.zh: 因條陳漢文時政以進。

translations.literal: He thereupon itemized Han Wen's policies of the time and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He then itemized Wen's policies of the time and presented them.

sentences.zh: 又言：「為國之道，在立法、任人二者而已。

translations.literal: He also said: "The way to govern a state lies in only two things: establishing law and appointing men.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Governing a state rests on two things alone: making laws and choosing men.

sentences.zh: 法不徒立，須人而行，人不濫用，惟賢是擇。」

translations.literal: Laws are not set up in vain—they require men to enforce them; men must not be misused—only the worthy are to be chosen."
translations.idiomatic: Laws cannot stand empty—they need men to carry them out; men must not be misused—only the worthy should be chosen."

sentences.zh: 因舉天下名士十餘人。

translations.literal: He thereupon recommended more than ten eminent men of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended more than ten eminent men under heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，皆召用，待以不次。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; all were summoned and employed with exceptional promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved; all were summoned and promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 三十年，遷國子司業。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred Director of Studies of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he became Director of Studies of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 有《彝齋文集》。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Works of the Yizhai Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Collected Works of the Yizhai Studio.

sentences.zh: 瑭子禮符。

translations.literal: Tang's son Lifu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's son Lifu.

sentences.zh: 仕為右衛屯田千戶。

translations.literal: He served as Thousand-Household of the Right Guard Colony Fields.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Thousand-Household of the Right Guard Colony Fields.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，謝病侍親，時年才三十二。

translations.literal: After a year he resigned on grounds of illness to attend his parents—he was only thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he pleaded illness to care for his parents—he was only thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 後還鄉里，築室曰晦道堂，蓋取七世祖宗弼，宋仁宗時為太子中舍人，年五十掛冠所築堂名也。

translations.literal: Later he returned home and built a hall called the Hall of Hidden Way, taking the name from his seventh-generation ancestor Zongbi, who in Emperor Renzong's time was Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and at fifty hung up his cap and built a hall of that name.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went home and built the Hall of Hidden Way, named for his seventh-generation ancestor Zongbi, who under Song Renzong had been Attendant to the Heir Apparent and at fifty resigned office and built a hall of that name.

sentences.zh: 趙良弼

translations.literal: Zhao Liangbi
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangbi

sentences.zh: 趙良弼，字輔之，女直人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangbi, styled Fuzhi, was a Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangbi, styled Fuzhi, was a Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 本姓術要甲，音訛為趙家，因以趙為氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Shuyao Jia; the sound was corrupted to Zhao family, and he therefore took Zhao as his clan name.
translations.idiomatic: His clan name was originally Shuyao Jia; corrupted in pronunciation to "Zhao family," he adopted Zhao as his surname.

sentences.zh: 父愨，金威勝軍節度使，諡忠閔；

translations.literal: His father Que was Jin Military Commissioner of Weisheng Army, posthumous title Zhongmin;
translations.idiomatic: His father Que was Jin Military Commissioner of Weisheng Army, posthumous title Loyal and Careful;

sentences.zh: 愨長子良貴，嵩汝招討使；

translations.literal: Que's eldest son Lianggui was Pacification Commissioner of Song and Ru;
translations.idiomatic: Que's eldest son Lianggui was Pacification Commissioner of Song and Ru;

sentences.zh: 良貴子讜，許州兵官；

translations.literal: Lianggui's son Dan was Xuzhou military officer;
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui's son Dan was military officer of Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 愨從子良材，守太原。

translations.literal: Que's cousin's son Liangcai held Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Que's cousin's son Liangcai held Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 俱死事。

translations.literal: All died in service.
translations.idiomatic: All died in the line of duty.

sentences.zh: 良弼明敏，多智略，初舉進士，教授趙州。

translations.literal: Liangbi was bright and keen, full of stratagems; he first passed the jinshi examination and taught in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi was sharp-witted and resourceful; after taking the jinshi degree he taught in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛籓，召見，佔對稱旨，會立邢州安撫司，擢良弼為幕長。

translations.literal: When the Khan was in his princely establishment he was summoned for audience; his divination answers pleased the throne; when the Xingzhou Pacification Commission was established he was promoted to chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: While the Khan was still heir apparent he was summoned; his prognostications pleased the prince, and when the Xingzhou Pacification Commission was set up he was made its chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 邢久不得善吏，且當要衝，使者旁午，民多逃去。

translations.literal: Xing had long lacked good officials, lay on a vital route, and envoys came and went without cease—many people fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xing had long gone without capable administrators, sat on a critical corridor with envoys passing constantly, and the people fled in numbers.

sentences.zh: 良弼區畫有方，事或掣制，則請諸籓邸，再閱歲，凡六往返，所請無不從。

translations.literal: Liangbi planned effectively; when affairs were obstructed he petitioned the princely residence—in less than a year he made six round trips and every request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi organized affairs with skill; when something was blocked he appealed to the princely residence, and within a year made six round trips—every petition was granted.

sentences.zh: 脫兀脫以斷事官鎮邢，其屬要結罪廢者，交構嫌隙，動相沮撓。

translations.literal: Toqtoq served as judicial officer in Xing; his subordinates who had been condemned for capital crimes wove suspicions and constantly thwarted one another.
translations.idiomatic: Toqtoq held judicial authority in Xing; subordinates condemned for capital crimes sowed suspicion and constantly obstructed one another.

sentences.zh: 世祖時徵雲南，良弼馳驛白其事，遂黜脫兀脫，罷其屬，邢大治，戶口增倍。

translations.literal: When the Khan was campaigning in Yunnan, Liangbi rode post-haste to report this; Toqtoq was dismissed and his subordinates removed—Xing was greatly well governed and households doubled.
translations.idiomatic: While the Khan campaigned in Yunnan, Liangbi rode post-haste to report the situation; Toqtoq was removed along with his men, Xing was thoroughly governed, and registered households doubled.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛籓時，分地在關陝，奏以廉希憲、商挺宣撫陝西，以良弼參議司事。

translations.literal: When the Khan held his princely establishment with territory in Guan and Long, he memorialized appointing Lian Xixian and Shang Ting to pacify Shaanxi and Liangbi to deliberate on commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his princely days, with territory in Guan and Long, he memorialized Lian Xixian and Shang Ting to pacify Shaanxi and Liangbi to serve as deliberator on commission affairs.

sentences.zh: 阿藍答兒當國，憚世祖英武，讒於憲宗。

translations.literal: When Alan Dar held power he feared the Khan's martial brilliance and slandered him to Möngke.
translations.idiomatic: When Alan Dar held sway he feared the Khan's prowess and slandered him to Möngke.

sentences.zh: 遂以阿藍答兒為陝西省左丞相，劉太平參知政事，鉤校京兆錢穀，煅煉群獄，死者二十餘人，眾皆股栗。

translations.literal: Alan Dar was then made Left Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat with Liu Taiping as Vice Director; they audited Jingzhao accounts and forged cases—more than twenty died and all trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Alan Dar was made Left Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat with Liu Taiping as Vice Director; they audited Jingzhao finances and fabricated prosecutions—more than twenty were executed and everyone trembled.

sentences.zh: 良弼力陳大義，詞氣懇款，二人卒不能誣，故宣撫司一無所坐。

translations.literal: Liangbi forcefully set forth the great principle with earnest words; the two could not frame him, so the Pacification Commission was not implicated at all.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi argued the great principle with earnest force; the two could not entrap him, and the Pacification Commission was not implicated.

sentences.zh: 己未七月，世祖南征，召參議元帥事，兼江淮安撫使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of jiwei the Khan campaigned south and summoned him to deliberate on marshal affairs, also as Huai-Huai Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of jiwei the Khan marched south, appointing him deliberator on marshal affairs and Huai-Huai Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 親執桴鼓，率先士卒，五戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He personally beat the drum and led the troops at the fore—five battles all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He himself beat the war drum, led from the front, and won five battles in succession.

sentences.zh: 禁焚廬舍、殺降民，所至宣布恩德，民皆按堵。

translations.literal: He forbade burning houses and killing surrendered civilians; wherever he went he proclaimed grace and the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade burning dwellings and killing those who surrendered; everywhere he proclaimed imperial kindness and the people were left in peace.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，攻鄂州，聞憲宗崩，世祖北還，良弼陳時務十二事，言皆有徵。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangtze they attacked Ezhou; hearing Möngke had died the Khan turned north—Liangbi presented twelve items on current affairs, all well founded.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river they attacked Ezhou; when Möngke's death was reported the Khan turned north, and Liangbi submitted twelve policy points, each well grounded.

sentences.zh: 至衛，遣如京兆察訪秦、蜀人情事宜，不踰月，具得實還報，曰：「宗王穆哥無他心，宜以西南六盤悉委屬之。

translations.literal: At Wei he was sent to Jingzhao to investigate conditions in Qin and Shu; within a month he returned with full report: "Prince Möngke has no other intent—the entire southwest Liupanshan should be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei he was sent to Jingzhao to survey Qin and Shu; within a month he returned with a full report: "Prince Möngke harbors no other design—the whole southwest Liupanshan should be placed under him.

sentences.zh: 渾都海屯軍六盤，士馬精強，咸思北歸，恐事有不意。

translations.literal: Hüntaihai garrisons Liupanshan with strong men and horses—all wish to return north; I fear something unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Hüntaihai holds Liupanshan with crack troops and horses eager to march north—I fear the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 紐璘總秦、川蒙古諸軍，多得秦、蜀民心，年少鷙勇，輕去就，當寵以重職，疾解其兵柄。

translations.literal: Niurong commands Mongol forces of Qin and Chuan and has won much popular hearts in Qin and Shu; young, fierce, and heedless of consequences—he should be honored with weighty office yet his military authority quickly removed.
translations.idiomatic: Niurong commands Qin and Chuan Mongol forces and has the hearts of Qin and Shu; young, fierce, and reckless—honor him with heavy rank but quickly strip his command.

sentences.zh: 劉太平、霍魯懷，今行尚書省事，聲言辦集糧餉，陰有據秦、蜀志。

translations.literal: Liu Taiping and Huoluai now conduct Branch Secretariat affairs, claiming to gather provisions yet secretly intending to hold Qin and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taiping and Huoluai now run Branch Secretariat affairs, claiming to gather rations while secretly plotting to hold Qin and Shu.

sentences.zh: 百家奴、劉黑馬、汪惟正兄弟，蒙被德惠，俱悉心俟命。」

translations.literal: Baijianu, Liu Heima, and the Wang Weizheng brothers have all received grace and await orders with full loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Baijianu, Liu Heima, and the Wang Weizheng brothers have all received favor and await orders faithfully."

sentences.zh: 其言皆見採用。

translations.literal: His words were all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Every point was adopted.

sentences.zh: 庚申，良弼凡五上言勸進，曰：「今中外皆願大王早進正宸，以安天下，事勢如此，豈容中止，社稷安危，間不容髮。」

translations.literal: In gengshen Liangbi five times memorialized urging accession: "Now within and without all wish Your Highness soon to take the throne and settle the realm—the momentum cannot be stopped; the realm's safety hangs by a hair."
translations.idiomatic: In gengshen Liangbi memorialized five times urging enthronement: "Within and without all wish you to take the throne soon and settle the realm—the moment cannot be lost; the state's safety hangs by a thread."

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: The Khan praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan approved.

sentences.zh: 既即位，立陝西四川宣撫司，復以廉希憲、商挺為使、副，良弼為參議。

translations.literal: Once enthroned he established the Shaanxi-Sichuan Pacification Commission, again appointing Lian Xixian and Shang Ting as commissioner and vice, Liangbi as deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he established the Shaanxi-Sichuan Pacification Commission with Lian Xixian and Shang Ting as commissioner and vice and Liangbi as deliberator.

sentences.zh: 良弼先行，謀諸斷事官八春曰：「今渾都海日夜思北歸，紐璘遷延不即行，當先遣使奉上旨促紐璘入朝，劉太平速還京兆。」

translations.literal: Liangbi went ahead and counseled Judicial Officer Bachu: "Now Hüntaihai thinks daily of returning north and Niurong delays departure—we should first send envoys with imperial orders to hurry Niurong to court and Liu Taiping quickly back to Jingzhao."
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi went ahead and told Judicial Officer Bachu: "Hüntaihai schemes daily to return north and Niurong tarries—first send envoys with imperial orders to hurry Niurong to court and Liu Taiping back to Jingzhao."

sentences.zh: 八春從其議。

translations.literal: Bachu followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bachu agreed.

sentences.zh: 至則紐璘果移營將入涇，劉太平將趨六盤，聞命乃止。

translations.literal: When they arrived Niurong had indeed moved camp toward Jing and Liu Taiping was rushing to Liupanshan—on receiving orders both stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Niurong had moved camp toward Jing and Liu Taiping was heading for Liupanshan—both halted on the orders.

sentences.zh: 後渾都海果叛北歸，良弼與汪惟正、劉黑馬二宣撫決議，執渾都海之黨元帥乞台不花、迷立火者誅之。

translations.literal: Later Hüntaihai did rebel northward; Liangbi with the two pacification commissioners Wang Weizheng and Liu Heima resolved to seize and execute Hüntaihai's partisans the commanders Qitai Buhua and Mili Huozhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Hüntaihai rebelled north, Liangbi with pacification commissioners Wang Weizheng and Liu Heima resolved to seize and execute his partisans the commanders Qitai Buhua and Mili Huozhe.

sentences.zh: 希憲及挺慮有擅殺名，遣使入奏待罪。

translations.literal: Xixian and Ting feared the charge of unauthorized killing and sent envoys to court to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian and Ting feared the stigma of unauthorized execution and sent envoys to court to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 良弼具密狀授使者，言：「始遣捕二帥時，止令囚以俟報，臣竊以為張惶不便，宜急誅之，擅殺在臣，實不在宣撫司，若上怒希憲等，願使者即出此奏。」

translations.literal: Liangbi gave the envoy a secret memorial saying: "When we first sent to seize the two commanders we only ordered imprisonment awaiting report—I thought delay unwise and that they should be executed at once; unauthorized killing lies with me, not the Pacification Commission—if Your Majesty is angry with Xixian and the rest, let the envoy produce this memorial at once."
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi gave the envoy a secret memorial: "When we seized the two commanders we meant only to hold them for report—I judged delay dangerous and urged immediate execution; the unauthorized killing is mine, not the commission's—if Your Majesty is angry with Xixian and others, produce this memorial now."

sentences.zh: 帝竟不問，使者以奏白政府，咸以良弼為長者。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end did not inquire; the envoy showed the memorial to the government and all regarded Liangbi as a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never pursued it; the envoy showed the memorial at court and all called Liangbi a man of honor.

sentences.zh: 升參議陝西省事。

translations.literal: He was promoted Deliberator of Shaanxi Branch Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Deliberator of Shaanxi Branch Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 蜀人費寅以私憾誣廉希憲、商挺在京兆有異志者九事，以良弼為徵。

translations.literal: The Shu man Fei Yin, from private grudge, accused Lian Xixian and Shang Ting of nine counts of disloyalty at Jingzhao, using Liangbi as witness.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu man Fei Yin, from private spite, accused Xixian and Ting of nine disloyal acts at Jingzhao, citing Liangbi as witness.

sentences.zh: 帝召良弼詰問，良弼泣曰：「二臣忠良，保無是心，願剖臣心以明之。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Liangbi to interrogate; Liangbi wept: "The two ministers are loyal—I know they have no such heart; I beg to cut open my heart to prove it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Liangbi and questioned him; he wept: "Both ministers are loyal—I know they have no such intent; cut open my heart to prove it."

sentences.zh: 帝意不釋。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was not eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was not persuaded.

sentences.zh: 會平李璮，得王文統交通書，益有疑二臣意，切責良弼，無所不至，至欲斷其舌。

translations.literal: When Li Tan was pacified and Wang Wentong's treasonous correspondence was found, suspicion of the two ministers grew; the emperor blamed Liangbi without limit, even wishing to cut out his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan was suppressed and Wang Wentong's treasonous letters surfaced, suspicion deepened; the emperor upbraided Liangbi relentlessly, even threatening to cut out his tongue.

sentences.zh: 良弼誓死不少變，帝意乃解，費寅卒以反誅。

translations.literal: Liangbi swore to die without changing; the emperor's mind was eased, and Fei Yin was finally executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi vowed to die rather than yield; the emperor relented, and Fei Yin was finally executed for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，以良弼為經略使，領高麗屯田。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan Liangbi was made Pacification Commissioner in charge of Goryeo colony fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan Liangbi was made commissioner overseeing Goryeo colony fields.

sentences.zh: 良弼言屯田不便，固辭，遂以良弼奉使日本。

translations.literal: Liangbi said colony fields were unsuitable and firmly declined; he was then sent as envoy to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi argued colony fields were impractical and firmly declined; he was then appointed envoy to Japan.

sentences.zh: 先是，至元初，數遣使通日本，卒不得要領，於是良弼請行。

translations.literal: Previously, from early Zhiyuan envoys had been sent repeatedly to Japan without gaining essentials, and Liangbi then asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: From early Zhiyuan envoys had gone to Japan repeatedly without success, and Liangbi volunteered.

sentences.zh: 帝憫其老，不許，良弼固請，乃授秘書監以行。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied his age and refused; Liangbi pressed his request and was granted Director of the Palace Library for the mission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied his age and refused; Liangbi insisted and was given the post of Palace Library Director for the journey.

sentences.zh: 良弼奏：「臣父兄四人，死事於金，乞命翰林臣文其碑，臣雖死絕域，無憾矣。」

translations.literal: Liangbi memorialized: "Four men of my father's and brothers' generation died in Jin service—I beg the Hanlin to compose their steles; though I die in a distant land I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi memorialized: "Father and brothers, four in all, died serving the Jin—I beg Hanlin scholars to write their steles; though I perish overseas I shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 帝從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 給兵三千以從，良弼辭，獨與書狀官二十四人俱。

translations.literal: Three thousand troops were given as escort; Liangbi declined and went only with twenty-four clerical officers.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand troops were offered; Liangbi refused and went with only twenty-four document officers.

sentences.zh: 舟至金津島，其國人望見使舟，欲舉刃來攻，良弼舍舟登岸喻旨。

translations.literal: When the boat reached Kin Island the Japanese saw the envoy vessel and wished to attack with blades—Liangbi left the boat and went ashore to announce the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: At Kin Island the Japanese saw the envoy ship and reached for weapons; Liangbi left the boat and went ashore to announce the imperial message.

sentences.zh: 金津守延入板屋，以兵環之，滅燭大噪，良弼凝然自若。

translations.literal: The Kin guard received him into a plank house, surrounded him with soldiers, extinguished lamps and shouted loudly—Liangbi remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: The Kin guard brought him into a plank house, ringed him with troops, put out the lamps and shouted—Liangbi remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 天明，其國太宰府官陳兵四山，問使者來狀。

translations.literal: At daybreak officials of the Dazaifu arrayed troops on four mountains and asked the envoy's business.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Dazaifu officials arrayed troops on four mountains and asked the envoy's purpose.

sentences.zh: 良弼數其不恭罪，仍喻以禮意。

translations.literal: Liangbi counted their disrespect and still instructed them in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi rebuked their disrespect yet still instructed them in proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 太宰官愧服，求國書。

translations.literal: The Dazaifu officials were ashamed and asked for the state letter.
translations.idiomatic: The Dazaifu officials were ashamed and asked for the imperial letter.

sentences.zh: 良弼曰：「必見汝國王，始授之。」

translations.literal: Liangbi said: "I must see your king before I can deliver it."
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi said: "I must see your king before handing it over."

sentences.zh: 越數日，復來求書，且曰：「我國自太宰府以東，上古使臣，未有至者，今大朝遣使至此，而不以國書見授，何以示信！」

translations.literal: After several days they came again for the letter, saying: "From Dazaifu eastward no ancient envoy has ever come; now the Great Court sends an envoy here—if you will not deliver the state letter, how can trust be shown!"
translations.idiomatic: Days later they returned, saying: "From Dazaifu east no envoy of antiquity has come; now the Great Court sends an envoy—without delivering the letter how can there be trust!"

sentences.zh: 良弼曰：「隋文帝遣裴清來，王郊迎成禮，唐太宗、高宗時，遣使皆得見王，王何獨不見大朝使臣乎？」

translations.literal: Liangbi said: "Emperor Wen of Sui sent Pei Qing and the king met him with suburban rites; under Taizong and Gaozong of Tang envoys all saw the king—why alone will you not receive a Great Court envoy?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi said: "Sui Wendi sent Pei Qing and your king met him with suburban rites; under Tang Taizong and Gaozong envoys all saw the king—why alone refuse a Great Court envoy?"

sentences.zh: 复索書不已，詰難往復數四，至以兵脅良弼。

translations.literal: They again demanded the letter without cease, arguing back and forth many times, even threatening Liangbi with arms.
translations.idiomatic: They demanded the letter again and again, arguing repeatedly, even threatening him with soldiers.

sentences.zh: 良弼終不與，但頗錄本示之。

translations.literal: Liangbi in the end would not give it, only showing them a partial copy.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi never yielded, only showing them a partial transcript.

sentences.zh: 後又聲言，大將軍以兵十萬來求書。

translations.literal: They again declared a great general would come with a hundred thousand men to demand the letter.
translations.idiomatic: They again claimed a great general would come with a hundred thousand men for the letter.

sentences.zh: 良弼曰：「不見汝國王，寧持我首去，書不可得也。」

translations.literal: Liangbi said: "Without seeing your king I would rather you take my head—the letter cannot be had."
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi said: "Without seeing your king you may take my head—the letter will not be given."

sentences.zh: 日本知不可屈，遣使介十二人入覲，仍遣人送良弼至對馬島。

translations.literal: Japan saw he could not be bent and sent twelve envoys to audience, also escorting Liangbi to Tsushima.
