translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not be broken, Japan sent twelve envoys to court and escorted Liangbi to Tsushima.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，良弼至自日本，入見，帝詢知其故，曰：「卿可謂不辱君命矣。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year Liangbi returned from Japan; at audience the emperor asked the cause and said: "You may be said not to have disgraced your commission."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year Liangbi returned; at audience the emperor heard the account and said: "You have not disgraced your sovereign's charge."

sentences.zh: 後帝將討日本，三問，良弼言：「臣居日本歲餘，睹其民俗，狠勇嗜殺，不知有父子之親、上下之禮。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor would campaign against Japan he asked three times; Liangbi said: "Your servant dwelt in Japan more than a year and observed their customs—fierce, murder-loving, ignorant of the bond between father and son or the rites of superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Later, planning war on Japan, the emperor asked three times; Liangbi said: "I lived in Japan more than a year and saw a people fierce and bloodthirsty, knowing neither filial piety nor hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 其地多山水，無耕桑之利，得其人不可役，得其地不加富。

translations.literal: Their land is mostly mountains and rivers without farming or sericulture—winning their people you cannot employ them, winning their land you do not grow richer.
translations.idiomatic: Their country is mountains and rivers without farming or sericulture—their people cannot be made to serve, their land adds no wealth.

sentences.zh: 況舟師渡海，海風無期，禍害莫測。

translations.literal: Moreover fleets cross the sea where winds have no season and disaster cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover fleets cross seas where winds are unpredictable and disaster incalculable.

sentences.zh: 是謂以有用之民力，填無窮之巨壑也，臣謂勿擊便。」

translations.literal: This is to pour useful human strength into a bottomless abyss—I advise not to attack."
translations.idiomatic: This is to pour useful strength into a bottomless pit—I advise against attack."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，以良弼同僉書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year Liangbi was made Associate Privy Council Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he was made Associate Privy Council Secretary.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏伐宋，良弼言：「宋重兵在揚州，宜以大軍先搗錢唐。」

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan campaigned against Song, Liangbi said: "Song's main force is at Yangzhou—the great army should first strike Qiantang."
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Bayan attacked Song, Liangbi said: "Song's main force holds Yangzhou—a great army should first strike Qiantang."

sentences.zh: 後訖如其計。

translations.literal: Later events proved exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved exactly as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 又言：「宋亡，江南士人多廢學，宜設經史科，以育人材，定律令，以戢姦吏。」

translations.literal: He also said: "With Song fallen, many Jiangnan scholars have abandoned learning—a classics and history examination should be established to nurture talent, and laws fixed to restrain corrupt officials."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "With Song gone, Jiangnan scholars have abandoned study—establish a classics and history examination to nurture talent and fix laws to curb corrupt officials."

sentences.zh: 卒皆用​​其議。

translations.literal: In the end all his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end all were adopted.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容問曰：「高麗，小國也，匠工弈技，皆勝漢人，至於儒人，皆通經書，學孔、孟。

translations.literal: The emperor once casually asked: "Goryeo is a small state, yet craftsmen and players surpass Han people; as for Ru scholars, all master the classics and study Confucius and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked casually: "Goryeo is small, yet artisans and players surpass Han people; its Ru scholars all master the classics and study Confucius and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 漢人惟務課賦吟詩，將何用焉！」

translations.literal: Han people only pursue tax levies and chanting poetry—what use are they!"
translations.idiomatic: Han people only chase taxes and compose poetry—of what use are they!"

sentences.zh: 良弼對曰：「此非學者之病，在國家所尚何如耳。

translations.literal: Liangbi answered: "This is not the fault of scholars but of what the state esteems.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi answered: "That is not scholars' fault but what the state honors.

sentences.zh: 尚詩賦，則人必從之，尚經學，則人亦從之。

translations.literal: If lyric poetry is honored, people will follow; if classical learning is honored, people will follow that too.
translations.idiomatic: Honor lyric poetry and people follow; honor the classics and people follow that.

sentences.zh: 良弼屢以疾辭，十九年，得旨居懷孟。

translations.literal: Liangbi repeatedly pleaded illness; in the nineteenth year he was permitted to reside in Huaimei.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi often pleaded illness; in the nineteenth year he was permitted to live in Huaimei.

sentences.zh: 良弼別業在溫縣，故有地三千畝，乃析為二，六與懷州，四與孟州，皆永隸廟學，以贍生徒，自以出身儒素，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: Liangbi's estate was in Wen County with three thousand mu of land; he divided it in two—six-tenths to Huai Prefecture, four-tenths to Meng Prefecture—all permanently assigned to temple schools to support students, showing himself a Ru by origin who did not forget his roots.
translations.idiomatic: His estate in Wen County held three thousand mu; he split it—six parts to Huai, four to Meng—all permanently for temple schools to support students, for he came from Ru stock and would not forget his roots.

sentences.zh: 或問為治，良弼曰：「必有忍，其乃有濟。

translations.literal: When asked about governing, Liangbi said: "There must be forbearance—only then can affairs succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about governing, he said: "There must be forbearance—only then is there success.

sentences.zh: 人性易發而難制者，惟怒為甚。

translations.literal: What in human nature is easy to burst forth and hard to control is above all anger.
translations.idiomatic: What bursts forth easily yet is hardest to control in human nature is anger.

sentences.zh: 必克己，然後可以制怒；

translations.literal: One must restrain oneself before one can master anger;
translations.idiomatic: Only by restraining oneself can one master anger;

sentences.zh: 必順理，然後可以忘怒。

translations.literal: one must follow principle before one can forget anger.
translations.idiomatic: only by following principle can one forget anger.

sentences.zh: 能忍所難忍，容所難容，事斯濟矣。」

translations.literal: To endure what is hard to endure and tolerate what is hard to tolerate—then affairs succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Endure the unbearable, tolerate the intolerable—then affairs succeed."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠翊運功臣、太保、儀同三司，追封韓國公，諡文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed Meritorious Minister Who Sincerely Assists in Transporting the Dynasty, Grand Guardian, Grand Master of the Palace with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes, posthumously Duke of Han with title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed Meritorious Minister of Sincere Counsel Who Assists the Dynasty, Grand Guardian, Grand Master of the Palace with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes, Duke of Han, posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 子訓，陝西平章政事。

translations.literal: His son Xun became Shaanxi Branch Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun became Shaanxi Branch Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 趙璧，字寶臣，雲中懷仁人。

translations.literal: Zhao Bi, styled Baochen, was a man of Huairen in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bi, styled Baochen, was from Huairen in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 世祖為親王，聞其名，召見，呼秀才而不名，賜三僮，給薪水，命後親製衣賜之，視其試服不稱，輒為損益，寵遇無與為比。

translations.literal: When the Khan was heir apparent he heard Bi's name, summoned him, called him Xiucai without using his personal name, granted three servants and stipend, ordered the consort to make clothes for him—when trial garments did not fit he altered them; favor unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: While heir apparent the Khan heard of Bi, summoned him, called him Xiucai without his personal name, gave three servants and stipend, had the consort make his clothes—if they did not fit he altered them; no one was favored like him.

sentences.zh: 命馳驛四方，聘名士王鶚等。

translations.literal: He ordered Bi to ride post-haste through the four directions to recruit eminent men such as Wang E.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bi post-haste through the realm to recruit eminent men such as Wang E.

sentences.zh: 又令蒙古生十人從璧受儒書。

translations.literal: He also had ten Mongol youths follow Bi to study Ru books.
translations.idiomatic: He also set ten Mongol youths to study Ru learning under Bi.

sentences.zh: 敕璧習國語，譯《大學衍義》，時從馬上聽璧陳說，辭旨明貫，世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He ordered Bi to study the national language and translate the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; often listening to Bi's exposition from horseback—the exposition was clear and the Khan praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Bi to learn the national language and translate the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; often he heard Bi expound from horseback—clear and praised by the Khan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，召璧問曰：「天下何如而治？」

translations.literal: When Möngke took the throne he summoned Bi and asked: "How may the realm be governed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke acceded he summoned Bi and asked: "How is the realm to be governed?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「請先誅近侍之尤不善者。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Please first execute the close attendants who are most unworthy."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "First execute the worst of the close attendants."

sentences.zh: 憲宗不悅。

translations.literal: Möngke was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Möngke was displeased.

sentences.zh: 璧退，世祖曰：「秀才，汝渾身是膽耶！

translations.literal: Bi withdrew; the Khan said: "Xiucai, your whole body is gall!
translations.idiomatic: Bi withdrew; the Khan said: "Xiucai, you are all gall!

sentences.zh: 吾亦為汝握兩手汗也。」

translations.literal: I too broke into a sweat for you."
translations.idiomatic: I too sweated for you with both hands."

sentences.zh: 一日，斷事官牙老瓦赤持其印，請於帝曰：「此先朝賜臣印也，今陛下登極，將仍用此舊印，抑易以新者耶？」

translations.literal: One day Judicial Officer Yalawachi held his seal and asked the emperor: "This is the seal the former dynasty granted me—now Your Majesty has ascended; shall I still use this old seal or receive a new one?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Judicial Officer Yalawachi brought his seal and asked: "This seal the former dynasty gave me—now that Your Majesty has ascended, shall I keep the old seal or receive a new one?"

sentences.zh: 時璧侍旁，質之曰：「用汝與否，取自聖裁，汝乃敢以印為請耶！」

translations.literal: Bi was attending and challenged him: "Whether to use you is the sacred decision—how dare you petition with the seal!"
translations.idiomatic: Bi stood by and rebuked him: "Whether to employ you is the sovereign's choice—how dare you bargain with your seal!"

sentences.zh: 奪其印，置帝前。

translations.literal: He seized the seal and placed it before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the seal and set it before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝為默然久之，既而曰：「朕亦不能為此也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent a long time, then said: "I too could not have done this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent long, then said: "I could not have done that myself."

sentences.zh: 自是牙老瓦赤不復用。

translations.literal: From then Yalawachi was never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: From then Yalawachi was never used again.

sentences.zh: 壬子，為河南經略使。

translations.literal: In renzi he was Henan Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In renzi he was Henan Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 河南劉萬戶貪婬暴戾，郡中婚嫁，必先賂之，得所請而後行，咸呼之為翁。

translations.literal: The Henan Ten-Thousand-Household Liu was greedy, lustful, and violent; in the commandery every marriage had first to bribe him—only after his price was met could the wedding proceed; all called him "Old Man."
translations.idiomatic: Henan's Ten-Thousand-Household Liu was greedy, lustful, and brutal; every wedding in the commandery had to bribe him first—only then could the marriage proceed; all called him "the Old Man."

sentences.zh: 其黨董主簿，尤恃勢為虐，強取民女有色者三十餘人。

translations.literal: His follower Registrar Dong was especially violent, forcibly taking more than thirty women of good appearance.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Registrar Dong was especially brutal, seizing more than thirty attractive women.

sentences.zh: 璧至，按其罪，立斬之，盡還民女。

translations.literal: When Bi arrived he investigated their crimes, executed Dong on the spot, and returned all the women to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi arrived he investigated, executed Dong immediately, and returned all the women.

sentences.zh: 劉大驚，時天大雪，因詣璧相勞苦，且酌酒賀曰：「經略下車，誅鋤強猾，故雪為瑞應。」

translations.literal: Liu was greatly alarmed; heavy snow was falling, so he came to Bi to offer condolences and raised a cup in congratulation: "Since the Pacification Commissioner took office and executed the violent and cunning, the snow is an auspicious response."
translations.idiomatic: Liu was terrified; snow was falling heavily, so he came to Bi with compliments and raised a cup: "Since you took office and cut down the strong and wicked, the snow is heaven's sign of approval."

sentences.zh: 璧曰：「如董主簿比者，尚有其人，俟盡誅之，瑞應將大至矣。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "Men like Registrar Dong still exist—when they are all executed, the auspicious sign will come in full."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said: "Men like Registrar Dong are still about—execute them all and the auspicious sign will be complete."

sentences.zh: 劉屏氣不復敢出語，歸臥病而卒，時人以為懼死。

translations.literal: Liu held his breath and dared speak no more; he returned home, took to his bed, and died—people thought he died of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu dared not speak again, went home, fell ill and died—people said he died of fright.

sentences.zh: 己未，伐宋，為江淮荊湖經略使。

translations.literal: In jiwei he campaigned against Song as Huai-Huai-Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei he campaigned against Song as Pacification Commissioner of Huai, Jiang, and Jing-Hu.

sentences.zh: 兵圍鄂州，宋賈似道遣使來，願請行人以和，璧請行。

translations.literal: The army besieged Ezhou; Song's Jia Sidao sent envoys asking for an envoy to negotiate peace—Bi asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: The army besieged Ezhou; Jia Sidao of Song sent envoys requesting a negotiator—Bi volunteered.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「汝登城，必謹視吾旗，旗動，速歸可也。」

translations.literal: The Khan said: "When you ascend the wall, watch My banner carefully—when the banner moves, return quickly."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "When you go up the wall, watch my banner—when it moves, come back at once."

sentences.zh: 璧登城，宋將宋京曰：「北兵若旋師，願割江為界，且歲奉銀、絹匹兩各二十萬。」

translations.literal: Bi ascended the wall; the Song general Song Jing said: "If the northern army withdraws, we wish to take the Yangtze as boundary and yearly present two hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk each."
translations.idiomatic: Bi went up the wall; Song general Song Jing said: "If the northern army withdraws, we will take the Yangtze as the border and yearly present two hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk each."

sentences.zh: 璧曰：「大軍至濮州時，誠有是請，猶或見從，今已渡江，是言何益！

translations.literal: Bi said: "When the great army reached Puzhou such a request might still have been granted; now we have crossed the river—of what use is this talk!
translations.idiomatic: Bi said: "When the great army reached Puzhou such terms might have been accepted; now we have crossed the river—what good is this talk!

sentences.zh: 賈制置今焉在耶？」

translations.literal: Where is Commissioner Jia now?"
translations.idiomatic: Where is Commissioner Jia now?"

sentences.zh: 璧適見世祖旗動，乃曰：「俟他日復議之。」

translations.literal: Just then Bi saw the Khan's banner move and said: "We shall discuss this another day."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Khan's banner move, Bi said: "We shall discuss this another day."

sentences.zh: 遂還。

translations.literal: He then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned.

sentences.zh: 高麗王禃為其臣林衍所逐，帝召璧還，改中書左丞，同國王頭輦哥行東京等路中書省事，聚兵平壤。

translations.literal: The Goryeo king Chung was driven out by his minister Lin Yan; the emperor recalled Bi, made him Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and with Prince Tianjegge conducted Branch Secretariat affairs of Tokyo and other routes, gathering troops at Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo king Chung was expelled by his minister Lin Yan; the emperor recalled Bi, made him Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and with Prince Tianjegge directed Branch Secretariat affairs in Tokyo and other routes, massing troops at Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 時衍已死，璧與王議曰：「高麗遷居江華島有年矣，外雖卑辭臣貢，內恃其險，故使權臣無所畏忌，擅逐其主。

translations.literal: Yan was already dead; Bi counseled the king: "Goryeo has dwelt on Jianghua Island for years; outwardly humble in words and tribute, inwardly relying on its defences—hence powerful ministers fear nothing and drive out their lord at will.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was already dead; Bi told the king: "Goryeo has lived on Jianghua Island for years—outwardly humble in tribute, inwardly trusting its defenses—so powerful ministers fear nothing and expel their king at will.

sentences.zh: 今衍雖死，王實無罪，若朝廷遣兵護歸，使復國於古京，可以安兵息民，策之上者也。」

translations.literal: Now though Yan is dead the king is truly innocent; if the court sends troops to escort him home and restore the realm at the ancient capital, troops can be stilled and the people pacified—this is the best policy."
translations.idiomatic: Yan is dead but the king is innocent; if the court sends troops to restore him at the ancient capital, war ceases and the people are pacified—that is the best course."

sentences.zh: 因遣使以聞，帝從之。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to report; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys to report; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時同行者分高麗美人，璧得三人，皆還之。

translations.literal: Companions on the mission divided Goryeo beauties; Bi received three and returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the mission divided Goryeo beauties among themselves; Bi received three and sent them all back.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷中書右丞。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was transferred Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，祀太廟，有司失黃幔，索得於神庖灶下，已甚污弊。

translations.literal: In winter at the Grand Temple sacrifice the officers lost the yellow curtain; it was found under the spirit kitchen stove, already filthy and worn.
translations.idiomatic: In winter at the Grand Temple sacrifice the officers lost the yellow curtain; it was found under the spirit kitchen stove, filthy and worn.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，大怒曰：「大不敬，當斬！」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and raged: "Great irreverence—they should be executed!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and raged: "Great irreverence—they should die!"

sentences.zh: 璧曰：「法止杖斷流遠。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "By law the limit is beating and exile."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said: "By law the penalty is beating and exile."

sentences.zh: 其人得不死。

translations.literal: The man was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The man was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 十年，復拜平章政事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was again appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was again Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，贈大司徒，諡忠亮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Minister of State with posthumous title Zhongliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dade he was posthumously made Grand Minister of State with posthumous title Loyal and Bright.

sentences.zh: 子二人：仁榮，同知歸德府事；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Rongrong, Associate Administrator of Guide Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Rongrong, Associate Administrator of Guide Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 仁恭，集賢直學士。

translations.literal: Ronggong, Direct Academician of the Hall of Collected Glories.
translations.idiomatic: Ronggong, Direct Academician of the Hall of Collected Glories.

sentences.zh: 孫二人：崇，郊祀署令；

translations.literal: Two grandsons: Chong, Director of the Suburban Sacrifice Office;
translations.idiomatic: Two grandsons: Chong, Director of the Suburban Sacrifice Office;

sentences.zh: 弘，左藏庫提點。

translations.literal: Hong, Superintendent of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, Superintendent of the Left Treasury.
